Shyam Kumar Mali vs Resham Baghel on 4 December, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Ind:35867
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Indore
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Alok Awasthi

On The 4 Th Of December, 2025
 Misc. Petition No. 4662 of 2025
 Shyam Kumar Mali
 Versus
 Resham Baghel And Others
 Appearance:
 Ms. Priyanka Bapna, Advocate for the petitioner.
 Shri Shyamlal Patidar, Advocate for the respondent No
 Shri Tejas Vyas, Advocate for the respondent No.3.
 Shri Pradeep Kumar Gupta, Advocate for the respondent
 Order

The petitioner has filed this miscellaneous petition under Article 227 of the Constitution of India challenging the order dated 30.07.2025 passed by the Member, MACT, Kukshi, District Dhar in Case No.MACC/43/2023, whereby, the Trial Court has allowed the application under Order 6 Rule 17 of CPC filed by the respondent No.4/defendant for amendment in the written statement alongwith cost of Rs.500/-.
2.

The facts as gathered from the pleadings brought on record reveals that respondent Nos.1 &
2/claimants filed a claim No.MACC/43/2023 claiming Rs.80.00 lacs as compensation for death of deceased Rahul Baghel, who was allegedly employed as a driver with the petitioner on his Bolero Pickup vehicle bearing No.MP11-G-6831.

On 03.08.2022, deceased NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:35867 2 MP-4662-2025 alongwith another driver i.e. respondent No.3 were transporting red chilly from Village Nipalagaon, Kukshi to Amarla, Gujarat.
When the said vehicle reached near Gola Gamdi Lothiya square on the Bodeli Dabhoi road, the vehicle met with an accident, which was driven by the respondent No.3 rashly and negligently.
Respondent No.3 escaped without any injury but Rahul sustained grievous injuries on his head and face, due to which he died on the spot.
The respondent No.4/Insurance Company filed its written statement.
3. The case is at the stage of final arguments.

At this stage, the respondent No.4/defendant filed an application under Order 6 Rule 17 of CPC seeking to amend his written statement, wherein the amendment in paras 2, 3 and 4 of the written statement is proposed.

The application for amendment filed alongwith petition reveals that the defendant is seeking permission to incorporate the amendment on the ground that at the time of filing reply, documents were in Gujarati language Shyam Kumar Mali vs Resham Baghel on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90328434/

sentences.text: The claimants filed a reply to this application and opposed the same by contending that the same has been filed at the stage of final arguments.
The policy in question was a package policy covering all statutory risks under Section 147 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

The Trial Court vide impugned order has allowed the application with a cost of Rs.500/- on the ground that though application has been filed at a belated stage but the proposed amendment will not cause prejudice to the other side nor alter the nature of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35867 3 MP-4662-2025 proceedings.

4. Challenging the impugned order of the Trial Court, counsel for the petitioner submitted that in view of proviso to Order 6 Rule 17 of CPC, the respondent No.4/defendant was required to show due diligence in filing the application for amendment.

Referring to the application, he submitted that the reason assigned for delay in filing the application is wholly unsatisfactory and unacceptable and,
therefore, application ought to have been rejected by the Trial Court.

5. On the other hand, counsel for the respondents supported the impugned order and submitted that the proposed amendment is only clarificatory in nature and does not cause prejudice to any party and therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition.

6. Considered the arguments and perused the record.
7.

Before adverting to the facts of this case, it is profitable to refer to the Apex Court judgement in the case of Abdul Rehman Vs. Mohd. Ruldu [(2012)3 MPWN 104], wherein the Apex Court has dealt with the scope of the provisions of Order 6 Rule 17 of CPC.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In para 8 & 14, it has been held as under :-
"8.

The original provision was deleted by Amendment Act 46 of 1999, however, it has again been restored by Amendment Act 22 of 2002 but with an added proviso to prevent application for amendment being allowed after the trial has commenced, unless the Court comes to the conclusion that in spite of due diligence, the party could not have raised the matter before the commencement of trial.
The above proviso, to some extent, curtails absolute discretion to allow amendment at any stage.
At present, if application is filed after commencement of trial, it has to be shown that in spite of due diligence, it could not have been sought earlier.

The object of the rule is that Courts should try the merits of the case that come before them and should, consequently, allow all amendments that may be necessary NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35867 4 MP-4662-2025 for determining the real question controversy between the parties provided it does not cause injustice or prejudice to the other side.
Court, in a series of decisions has that the power to allow the amendment is wide and can be exercised at any stage of the proceeding in the interest of justice.

The main purpose of allowing the amendment is to minimize the litigation and the plea that the relief sought by way of amendment was barred by time is to be considered in the light of the facts and circumstances of each case.

The above principles have been reiterated by this Court in J. Samuel and Others vs. Gattu Mahesh and Others, (2012) 2 SCC 300 and Rameshkumar Agarwal vs. Rajmala Exports Pvt. Ltd. and Others, (2012) 5 SCC 337.

sentences.text: In Pankaja & Anr. vs. Yellapa (Dead) By Lrs. & Ors. AIR 2004 SC 4102: (2004) 6 SCC 415, this Court held that if the granting of an amendment really subserves the ultimate cause of justice and avoids further litigation, the same should be allowed.

entities.text: Pankaja & Anr. vs. Yellapa (Dead) By Lrs. & Ors. AIR 2004 SC 4102: (2004) 6 SCC 415
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the same decision, it was further held that an amendment seeking declaration of title shall not introduce a different relief when the necessary factual basis had already been laid down in the plaint in regard to the title."
8. In view of the aforesaid legal proposition, it is clear that effort of the Court should be to grant the amendment if it serves the ultimate cause of justice.
The another aspect to be looked into is, as to whether any serious prejudice is caused to any party.

As seen from the application for amendment,
the respondent No.4 has proposed amendment in paras 2, 3 and 4 of written statement which does not incorporate any new fact and only clarifies the averments already made in the written statement.
9. Thus, counsel for the petitioner is correct while stating that the explanation given by the respondent No.4 for explaining the delay is unsatisfactory.
The reasons assigned cannot be a ground for not making the amendment earlier.

10. The Apex Court has discussed about the scope of interference of this Court under Article 227 of the Constitution of India in the case of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35867 5 MP-4662-2025 Estralla Rubber Vs. Dass Estate (P) Ltd., [(2001) 8 SCC 97] , wherein in para - 6, the Apex Court has held as under:-
"6.

entities.text: NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35867 5 MP-4662-2025 Estralla Rubber Vs. Dass Estate (P) Ltd., [(2001) 8 SCC 97]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The scope and ambit of exercise of power and jurisdiction by a High Court under Article 227 of the Constitution of India is examined and explained in number of decisions of this Court.

The exercise of power under this Article involves a duty on the High Court to keep inferior courts and tribunals within the bounds of their authority and to see that they do duty expected or required by them in a legal manner.
The High Court is not vested with any unlimited prerogative to correct all kinds of hardship or wrong decisions made within the limits of the jurisdiction of the courts subordinate or tribunals.

Exercise of this power and interfering with the orders of the courts or tribunal is restricted to cases of serious dereliction of duty and flagrant violation of fundamental principles of law or justice, where if High Court does not interfere, a grave injustice remains uncorrected.

It is also well settled that the High Court while acting under this Article cannot exercise its power as an appellate court or substitute its own judgment in place of that of the subordinate court to correct an error, which is not apparent on the face of the record.

The High Court can set aside or ignore the findings of facts of inferior court or tribunal, if there is no evidence at all to justify or the finding is so perverse, that no reasonable person can possibly come to such a conclusion, which the court or Tribunal has come to."
11.
In view of the aforesaid discussions, this petition is allowed and the impugned order is set aside.
The respondent No.4/Insurance Company is at liberty to take his defence with respect to proposed amendment at the time of final arguments.
